projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The steady rise to 22 connected devices combined with zero camera motion at 1:26 AM strongly suggests either guests have settled into sleep in camera-blind zones or the presence tracker is miscounting stationary IoT devices as mobile phones. A quick verification of actual occupancy or sensor calibration is recommended to rule out tracking errors or ensure everyone's safety.

The sustained presence of ~19-20 devices paired with zero camera motion for four hours strongly suggests a large group of guests is present but confined to camera-blind zones or remaining very still, likely for a movie or gaming session. The device count increase at 23:30 indicates a possible late arrival, so a quick verification is recommended to ensure everyone is accounted for.

The sustained presence of 19 devices with zero camera motion over four hours suggests either a gathering confined to a single area outside camera coverage or a potential camera system fault; verifying camera functionality and confirming expected guests is recommended.

The sustained ~20-device presence paired with zero camera motion over four hours, especially at 10:22 PM with children and active dogs in the home, strongly indicates a camera system malfunction or disabled motion detection rather than normal evening stillness; verifying camera functionality and confirming household status is recommended.

The sustained presence of ~20 mobile devices over four hours combined with zero camera motion strongly suggests a stationary gathering of guests in a camera-blind area or a network counting anomaly; verify if unexpected visitors are present or if network sensors need recalibration.

The consistent ~20-device network presence paired with zero camera activity over four hours indicates the security cameras are likely offline or malfunctioning, leaving the home unmonitored during prime evening hours when motion is expected.

The sustained 19-21 device count with zero camera activity over four hours, despite repeated flags, confirms a stable IoT device baseline rather than human activity or a security event, indicating no new action is needed beyond routine network monitoring.

Sustained network presence of 20-22 devices combined with zero camera activity over four hours strongly suggests the camera system is offline, disabled, or malfunctioning rather than the house being empty, as the device count aligns with a full household. This matters because it leaves the home unmonitored during typical evening activity hours.

The sustained 21-23 device network count paired with zero camera activity over 90 minutes indicates the presence metric is likely inflated by stationary IoT devices rather than actual people, suggesting the household is in a camera-blind zone or low-activity state. This matters because automations relying on presence data may be triggering incorrectly or masking real occupancy changes.

Network presence jumped from 17 to 23 devices between 14:12 and 14:38 with zero corresponding camera activity, suggesting new devices connected without triggering motion sensors—likely indicating guests arriving outside or a network shift worth verifying.
